newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hannover Re in joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Hannover Re in joint venture.

text.p: German reinsurer Hannover Rueckversicherung (Hannover Re) has set up a joint venture with American capital markets specialist Derrell Hendrix and an as-yet unnamed European bank, the company said on Monday.

RISConsulting Group LLC is based in Boston and offers consultancy services for reinsurers, primary insurers, industrial companies, banks and others in the field of risk transfer and insurance derivatives including development, realisation and marketing.
Derrell Hendrix, who spent 18 years with Citibank and a short spell with Bank of Boston, holds 50 percent of the new company.

Hannover Re owns 25 percent via its Los Angeles-based subsidiary Insurance Corporation of Hannover. The name of the bank to join the company would be revealed later this week, but it was "one of the few AAA banks in Europe", said Dirk Lohmann of Hannover Re's management board. The bank would hold probably "just below 20 percent".

Hendrix was regarded as a leading expert in the field of derivatives and risk management and structuring, Lohmann said. He and his associates would eventually own just above 50 percent of the new company.

Other managers of the company include Joseph Blundo, a banker and business consultant, Martin Veasy, who was in-house risk specialist for Price Waterhouse in London, Ren Wu, who worked for Citibank in derivatives, and Kerstin Hendrix, who was a stock research analyst with Enskilda Securities.

Hannover Re, which with premium income of more than six billion marks is the world's fifth largest reinsurer, also announced that it closed a second transaction in the alternative risk transfer market on 22 November.

Through a portfolio-linked swap involving U.S. institutional investors, it arranged 100 million dollars in risk capital for five to seven years. Investors receive a high dividend if the loss ratio for a certain area remains below a pre-defined line, but lose some of their money if the loss ratio exceeds another line.
